title: Surjective comparison from successive module strict transforms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, and $b:S_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(S)\to S$ its blowup. Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_{S_1}$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal and $c:S_2=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(S_1)\to S_1$ its blowup [def-pc-scheme], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Set $Z=V(\mathcal I)$ and $Z_1=V(\mathcal J)$. Suppose a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K$ on $S$ and an isomorphism $S_2\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(S)$ over $S$ are specified, with $V(\mathcal K)=Z\cup b(Z_1)$ as subsets. Let $f:X\to S$ be any morphism and $\mathcal F$ any quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Write $X_i=X\times_SS_i$, $p:X_1\to X$, $q:X_2\to X_1$, $f_2:X_2\to S_2$, and $H=(p\circ q)^*\mathcal F\cong q^*p^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $\mathcal F_1$ be the module strict transform along $b$, $\mathcal F_2$ its module strict transform along $c$, and $\mathcal G$ the module strict transform of $\mathcal F$ along the specified $\mathcal K$-blowup, transported to $X_2$ [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. These modules are quasi-coherent. The composite of the pulled-back first quotient with the second quotient is an epimorphism $\alpha:H\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F_2$. For the canonical epimorphism $\beta:H\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal G$ and $D=(bc\circ f_2)^{-1}V(\mathcal K)$, one has $\ker\alpha\subseteq\ker\beta$ and a unique epimorphism $\theta:\mathcal F_2\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal G$ with $\theta\alpha=\beta$; every local section of its kernel is supported on $D$.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, proof paragraphs 1--2: composite quotient, containment of kernels, and the surjective comparison; module clause (1).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-iterated-transform-quotient-support] with $b_0=b$, $b_1=c$, $M=\mathcal F_1$ and $N=\mathcal F_2$. It gives quasi-coherence of $\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2$ and the stated epimorphism $\alpha$, using the specified identification $H\cong q^*p^*\mathcal F$. Put $T_I=(bc f_2)^{-1}Z$ and $T_J=(c f_2)^{-1}Z_1$. The same lemma says $\alpha$ is an isomorphism off $T_I\cup T_J$ and its kernel sections vanish there. Apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] to the specified $\mathcal K$-blowup and $\mathcal F$. On $X_2$ this gives quasi-coherence of $\mathcal G$, the epimorphism $\beta$, and $\ker\beta$ equal to all local sections of $H$ zero off $D$; also $\beta$ is an isomorphism off $D$.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, proof paragraphs 1--2 (through the factorization); Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1).

proof.text: Since $V(\mathcal K)=Z\cup b(Z_1)$, one has $T_I\subseteq D$. If $x\in T_J$, then $c f_2(x)\in Z_1$, hence $bc f_2(x)\in b(Z_1)\subseteq V(\mathcal K)$, so $T_J\subseteq D$. For every open $W\subseteq X_2$ and $s\in(\ker\alpha)(W)$, [lem-trf-iterated-transform-quotient-support] gives $s|_{W\setminus(T_I\cup T_J)}=0$. Restricting further gives $s|_{W\setminus D}=0$. The kernel description of [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] therefore gives $s\in(\ker\beta)(W)$. This proves $\ker\alpha\subseteq\ker\beta$ as subsheaves.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, proof paragraphs 1--2 (through the factorization); Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1).

proof.text: Define $\theta$ by local lifts: for a local section $t$ of $\mathcal F_2$, choose an open cover and sections $h_i$ of $H$ with $\alpha(h_i)=t|_{W_i}$, and set $\theta(t)|_{W_i}=\beta(h_i)$. Differences of lifts lie in $\ker\alpha\subseteq\ker\beta$, so the values agree on overlaps, are independent of the lifts, and glue. This also proves linearity, compatibility with restrictions and $\theta\alpha=\beta$. Any such map has these values, so is unique. Every section of $\mathcal G$ locally lifts along the epimorphism $\beta$; its lift $h$ yields the preimage $\alpha(h)$ under $\theta$. Thus $\theta$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, proof paragraphs 1--2 (through the factorization); Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1).

proof.text: By $T_I\cup T_J\subseteq D$ and step 1, both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ restrict to isomorphisms on $X_2\setminus D$. There $\theta=\beta\alpha^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. If $t$ is any local section of $\ker\theta$ on an open $W$, its restriction to $W\setminus D$ is consequently zero. This is precisely the asserted support condition on its kernel.
